ruleName: Ball Deflected by Person Attending or Holding Up Flagstick or Anything Else
imagePrompt: A semi-realistic, polished illustration in a modern junior golf quiz style, showing a putting green scene: Mark is putting with his ball rolling towards the hole, while Rachel is shown intentionally replacing the flagstick into the hole just as the ball approaches. Focus on body language to show Rachel’s deliberate action and Mark’s ongoing putt. Background should clearly indicate a golf green and hole location, with realistic but slightly stylised vibrant greens and natural light. Do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: Rachel deliberately replacing the flagstick in the hole while Mark’s golf ball is rolling towards the hole on the putting green.

sceneSpec.setting: Putting green near a flagstick and hole
sceneSpec.players: Two players: Rachel and Mark. Mark is putting, Rachel is near the hole.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: Mark’s ball is rolling on the green towards the hole; the flagstick is being put back into the hole by Rachel.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: Moment when Rachel is replacing the flagstick while Mark's ball is in motion on the green.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Whether a player may deliberately replace the flagstick while an opponent’s ball is in motion in match play.
mustShow: Rachel intentionally replacing the flagstick in the hole (hand visible on flagstick)
Mark in the process of putting with ball rolling towards the hole
The flagstick in the act of being returned to the hole

questions.title: Putting and the Flag in a Match
questions.question: Rachel and Mark are playing a match. While Mark is trying to putt, Rachel puts the flagstick back in the hole on purpose. Mark’s ball then hits the flagstick. What happens?
questions.explanation: If you put the flagstick back in the hole on purpose while your friend’s ball is rolling, and the ball then hits the flagstick, you lose that hole in match play.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The tall stick that goes in the hole to show where it is on the green.
A game of golf where you try to win more holes than your friend, not count all your shots for the whole round.

questions.teachingTip: Remind children to wait until everyone has finished putting before touching the flagstick, so no one is distracted or gets in trouble.
likelyMisconceptions: It’s okay to put the flag back while someone is putting if you think it will help them.
Nothing happens if the ball hits the flag after you put it back during someone else’s putt.

questions.title: Replacing the Flag during a Putt in Match Play
questions.question: In match play, Rachel deliberately replaces the flagstick in the hole while Mark is putting. Mark’s putt is then deflected by the flagstick. What is the ruling?
questions.explanation: Under Rule 11.8, in match play, if a player deliberately takes an action to affect a ball in motion (for example, replacing the flagstick while an opponent’s ball is rolling towards the hole), they lose the hole.
